**Myth: mathematicians crying over AI is just bruised ego.**

Derek Thompson argues they're mourning the human conversation of discovery.

Fields medalist Hugo Duminil-Copin: "They have annihilated my field of research."

I think programmers face the same question about solving things ourselves.

**Grief or bruised ego? Pick a side, then save this.**
bullets: Strogatz at Cornell describes "enormous grief" in his field.
Thompson grants some ego, but says AI is "interrupting the thousand-year conversation."
One developer disagreed: "almost all bruised egos and feeling of wasted time."
